#1554. Newcastle 2-2 Arsenal: Two points dropped in a game of two halves

In the cold light of day, it’s hard not to look at what happened in the 45th minute of this game as a key moment. Arsenal were 1-0 up, well on top and absolutely deserving of the lead. Newcastle had struggled to exert any kind of control, and we’d already had 9 attempts on goal.

A good move down the left hand side saw Martin Odegaard square perfectly for Noni Madueke who arrived with pace, ready to finish first time. Unfortunately for him and for us, Lewis Hall produced a quite outstanding piece of defending to slide in and block the shot over the bar. That was the difference between Arsenal going in 2-0 up at the break rather than with just the single goal margin.

The lead had come via Eberechi Eze, finishing emphatically after superb work from Kai Havertz to rob the ball and play a deft pass behind the right back. Newcastle’s only chance had come early, a shot from Jacob Murphy that deflected off his own player and drifted wide with David Raya wrong-footed. After that, we bossed the half, with 11 shots in total, 65% possession, but still only that one goal.

It feels redundant to say this is a very, very good Arsenal team, but if we have a weakness, it’s that we don’t turn this kind of domination into more goals. Very often we don’t need to as our defensive solidity and consistency keeps the opposition at bay, but last night we let our standards slip in that regard, and the lack of firepower or being clinical in the final third came home to roost.

It was, very literally, a game of two halves. Newcastle made a triple sub at the break and it would be churlish not to give them credit for the fact it made a positive impact. However, the Arsenal performance was night and day. The opposition upped the energy and intensity, and we made mistakes. Odegaard miskicking a Riccardo Calafiori throw-in provided them the opportunity to equalise, and I do wonder why Harvey Barnes was so free at the back post to slide home for 1-1.

That goal gave them momentum, they caused us problems again and again, some of them of our own making with carelessness and misfortune. Eze got back well to defend in our box but unfortunately slipped, Raya’s clearance was unconvincing and then Gabriel had to boot the ball behind for a corner – from which they made it 2-1. Dan Burn drifted off Jurrien Timber to get a free header, the ball scrambled around a bit before Malick Thiaw poked it over the line to give them the lead. Messy, shambolic defending – not very Arsenal at all.

If we’re being fair, we have to say they could have scored again. David Raya went off with a shoulder injury, Kepa had to make a smart save at the feet of Lewis Miley but why was he one on one with the keeper in the first place? A Joe Willock shot deflected wide in similar fashion to the Murphy one in the first half, and eventually Arteta changed things with Christos Tzolis and Myles Lewis-Skelly coming on for Eze and Bruno Guimaraes who had a quiet return to his former club – bar that first half moment when he almost got enough contact on a fantastic Declan Rice cross but could only put the ball wide from close range.

We did get an equaliser, and very well worked it was too. We played the ball across the back line from right to left, into midfield where Havertz’s smart dummy allowed Odegaard room to drive on and find Madueke. He was Arsenal’s best attacking player last night, he kept trying to make things happen, and while I think the Newcastle keeper will probably have nightmares about letting that shot in, Madueke deserved the goal, and it earned us a point.

It was after the 90th minute when the manager brought on Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino to try and find a winner, the Swede had one shot over the bar from the edge of the box, but had we found another, it would have been a real smash and grab. In the end, the draw was probably a fair result based on how the game played out, and afterwards the manager was unhappy at leaving two points behind:

My feeling is that we have lost two points today. And I say we because we were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. It should have been two, three or four-nil up, clear. But it wasn’t.

We started to lose duels, we started to lose second balls. We gave the ball away and have really poor circulation balls against their press and their waves. And when that happens, you give them belief.

It’s a pity because the margin should have been, again, much bigger for the level that we’ve shown.

And this is the key for me. It should have been, but it wasn’t, and it too often isn’t. As I said above, our defensive brilliance is fundamental to us winning so many games, but football is a game of variance. You can’t always control everything. On another night Odegaard just puts his foot through that throw in and that first Newcastle goal doesn’t happen. Eze and Raya deal better with that situation and we don’t concede a corner. We can focus on those individual things and say we could and should do better for sure, but you have to allow for some of that over the course of a season. You cannot be perfect for 90+ minutes 38 games in every league campaign.

The ongoing issue for me is our firepower though. I thought generally the front three played pretty well last night, and it’s not as if we missed a glut of chances, but it’s about turning the level of dominance we had in that first half into more goals. This isn’t a one-time issue either. We scored two lovely goals last night but we should have had that game firmly in our grasp at half-time, but in this league a single goal margin is never a sure thing.

The summer was a let-down in an attacking sense, there’s no getting away from that. If we had a forward line that was even close to our midfield and defence in terms of quality and depth, the Premier League would be a cakewalk. I know that’s a bit simplistic, but it’s also a fact. Regardless of what you think of the business, we let goals go to Turkey and Saudi Arabia, and replaced them with a player who has yet to score. Which isn’t to lay the blame at the feet of Tzolis, far from it, but with the squad planning/building that was undertaken.

For me, January becomes increasingly important because the improvement required is obvious, and for a sporting director whose track record looks quite hit and miss as it is, he needs a convincing window or the questions around the job he’s doing will become louder and louder, and for good reason.

The other big issue from yesterday was the injury to David Raya. It didn’t look good at all, and any absence for him would be a huge blow to the team. He’s been the best in the Premier League, and perhaps the best in Europe, for the last 18 months, and inevitably there’s a drop-off when any club is without their first choice keeper for any period of time. That’s another adjustment we’re probably going to have to make, and if it means we’re likely to be less secure and clean sheets are harder to come by, then that issue of scoring goals and being more potent comes into even sharper focus. Let’s keep fingers crossed it’s not as bad as it appears to be.

Right, I’ll leave it there for now. There’s plenty to unpick from this one, so I’ll leave you to it in the Arses. More here tomorrow, including an Arsecast Extra. Until then, have a great Sunday.

#1553. Mind the gap

Over the last few weeks, I’ve grown accustomed to waking up and experiencing low-level fear first thing in the morning. Today, it was a nice change not to be focused on my own health, and instead for my anxiety to centre around someone else – David Raya.

With any team or any squad there are players whose absence will be more keenly felt than others, but one of the things Arsenal have generally done really well in the last few years is close the gaps between ‘first choice’ and those behind them. It doesn’t mean there isn’t still a kind of hierarchy, just that you’re better able to cope if injury or suspension hits. Mikel Arteta referencing ‘finishers’ rather than substitutes might be a psychological ploy to keep his squad happy, but it’s more easy to apply when you have the group of players he has at his disposal.

If Jurrien Timber is out, we have Ben White. If Riccardo Calafiori can’t play, Piero Hincapie can. We all worried about William Saliba needing a long lay-off after the World Cup, but the arrival of Ezri Konsa offset that in exemplary fashion. If we miss Declan Rice, we have two World Cup winners, a Brazilian international, and one of the most highly regarded young English midfielders around to fill that gap. Further forward, Noni Madueke is performing at a level that makes Bukayo Saka’s absence feel less impactful than it would have previously, and while I think forward line quality remains an issue we need to solve as urgently as January, you can flip a coin between most of our options there without feeling you’ve weakened yourself considerably.

Unfortunately, I don’t think the same applies between the sticks. Raya has been the stand-out goalkeeper of the last few years, establishing himself as Arsenal’s number 1 after an initial settling in period. One, by the way, which I don’t think the manager handled particularly well. Typically he’s been near flawless in terms of his man-management, and while he was fundamentally right about wanting the Spaniard to come in and take the position to a new level, the way he fudged things around Aaron Ramsdale, talking about how he’d sub a goalkeeper in a game and all that nonsense really wasn’t his best moment. It left both of his keepers in a weird place for too long, until Raya’s confidence grew and his quality came to the fore.

Since then he’s won multiple golden glove awards, his shot-stopping has been incredible at times, and although every player and every keeper will make mistakes, his have been few and far between. For me though, despite the eye-catching acrobatics – which are more easily clipped up for the social media generation – his key asset is the assurance he brings to the team. Not just when he has the ball at his feet (even if there are times I would like him to move it more quickly), but how good he is from opposition set-pieces and crosses. He comes and claims and eases pressure time and time again, and I think that’s the thing we’re going to miss most if he’s out for any significant period of time.

Kepa is obviously a very experienced second choice, but is second choice for a reason. Realistically though, I don’t think there’s much any club can do to have a back-up option that’s nearly as good as their number 1. If you’re being brutally honest, many clubs in the Premier League don’t have a first choice that comes anywhere close to be as good as Raya, despite their best efforts and spending millions to try and find that player. So, as anxious as I am about him being out, it is one of those things we can’t really complain about. We just have to get on with it.

As I said in yesterday’s blog, we are probably going to be less secure at the back, that feels kind of inevitable, so the onus on the players further forward increases. Score more goals, turn that domination of possession and territory into more chances. If we have the ball in their half, our goalkeeper becomes something of a non-issue for as long as that’s the case. There are ways to cope, but we might need to gird our loins for some iffy moments at the back that we haven’t had to experience too often of late.

As Arsenal fans though, we’ve come through worse than this with goalkeepers in the past. I don’t want to give anyone PTSD first thing on a Monday morning, but when you’ve lived what we’ve lived in seasons gone by, hopefully a little Kepa period won’t be too traumatic. And maybe, after the scan, there’ll be better news about Raya than we expect. Fingers crossed.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

Pod should be out around noon. Until then!

#1552. Columbus Crew vs Inter Miami - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:16, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:19

On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.

Columbus had a lot of momentum heading into the playoffs, and that continued on Saturday as they took advantage of some sloppy Miami defending to take a surprising lead in this series.

Laurent Courtois has seen his side score three or more goals in four of their last five matches versus MLS opposition, while posting a clean sheet in three of those instances, making them an appealing option to choose on the UK betting sites

The Crew exposed gaps in the Miami squad, scoring on three of their five targeted efforts last weekend and putting the Herons on the ropes heading into game two.

This is only the second time they are up 1-0 since this best-of-three first-round format was introduced, with this team advancing past Atlanta United in three games on the only previous occasion in which they were in this position in 2023.

Only once since their 2015 MLS Cup final defeat versus the Portland Timbers have they lost a post-season match at home, with the New York Red Bulls blanking them 1-0 in game one of that opening round series in 2024.

Friday will mark the second time the Crew can eliminate Miami from a major competition in Columbus, after knocking them out of the 2024 Leagues Cup thanks to a 3-2 victory at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in the round of 16.

For a team boasting so much experience and talent in the biggest club and international competitions, Inter Miami failed to keep their composure in numerous instances last weekend.

Saturday’s defeat was the joint-worst for the club in the post-season, though given everything that transpired, they could be looking much worse heading into this match.

Kily Gonzalez will be relieved to know that Lionel Messi is available, escaping with just a caution in game one after throwing the ball at Gonzalo Tapia, a moment some believed should have warranted a sending off for the Argentine.

Miami played a good portion of that match a man down, and have never won the second game in a best-of-three MLS playoff series.

The Herons have given up a combined six goals in their last two matches versus MLS opposition and have yet to beat an MLS club in a knockout fixture this season.

The reigning league champions have lost four of their five all-time playoff outings away from home, with their only triumph coming at FC Cincinnati in 2025 (4-0).

Due to a cruciate ligament tear, Wessam Abou Ali will not be available for Columbus in game two of this series.

Gonzalo Tapia netted twice in Miami, with Taha Habroune also scoring as Patrick Schulte made three stops for the clean sheet.

On the Miami side, Mateo Silvetti is dealing with a shoulder issue, Tadeo Allende still has a knee problem and Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Gonzalo Lujan will be suspended following his red card in game one, while Sergio Reguilon, David Ayala and Cesar Abadia are all questionable with lower-body injuries.

Schulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zaroury, Chambost, Habroune, Rodriguez, Tapia, Mendez

St. Clair; Fray, Casemiro, Micael, Falcon; De Paul, Bright, Segovia; Messi, Suarez, Berterame

While Miami have all they need to come back and win this series, they are far too rigid defensively and give away too many quality scoring opportunities, which is why we believe their season will end much earlier than most would have expected.

#1551. Opinion: Liverpool's new transfer plans will mark the end for Jurgen Klopp favourite

Liverpool have a lot of work to still do on their squad.

Andoni Iraola took charge of the club just after they delivered an extremely shoddy title defence.

They ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League which resulted in them spending another £150 million on new players.

And, while some of those transfers have worked out, it still feels like one or two, such as Bradley Barcola, still have a lot to live up to.

Obviously, as each season goes on, clubs try to add new players to their ranks and, since Liverpool's Premier League title rivals will be doing this, the Reds need to figure out ways to improve their ranks and get back to their best.

Unfortunately, for some of Liverpool's players, this means that their time at Anfield will need to be brought to an end.

On Monday evening, Anfield Watch revealed that Liverpool are eyeing a move for Abdellah Ouazane.

The 17-year-old is currently plying his trade for Ajax in the Eredivisie and, despite being so young, he's already featured in 20 games for the Dutch outfit this term.

During those games, he's contributed to eight goals across all competitions and he has also been played in an array of positions.

The Moroccan was properly promoted to their first-team squad this term after Mika Godts accepted a move to PSG.

Indeed, Ouazane did feature for Ajax once in their domestic cup last season but, this term is the first where he's been a regular part of Miguel Ángel Sánchez Muñoz's team.

To make the deal even sweeter and even more likely, Ouazane is actually a Liverpool fan so, if the Reds went in for him, there's very little chance that he'd say no.

Abdellah Ouazane joining Liverpool would confirm Harvey Elliott's exit

Right now, Liverpool don't really have a proper back-up for Florian Wirtz.

The young German has been the Reds' number 10 for most of the season with James McConnell taking over the role in some of Liverpool's cup games.

And, while McConnell has done a decent job, it's clear that the Reds need to start thinking about having a genuine back-up for Wirtz among their ranks.

Harvey Elliott was probably hoping that would be his role this term but, instead, he's been sent out on loan again.

His time with Valencia started off fairly poorly but, now, he's finally starting to find his feet with his main goal for the campaign likely to be get back on the good side of Iraola.

But, unfortunately for the Englishman, who was often one of the first names on Jurgen Klopp's team sheet, these recent links with Ouazane more or less confirm that his future lies away from Anfield.

That is, unless he can become Valencia's best player and start contributing to goals again.

Published: 11:10 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:10 EST, 23 November 2026

Footage has emerged of Ange Postecoglou locked in a fiery exchange with a reporter after Al-Nassr's defeat to Al-Ahli - after he questioned Sadio Mane's commitment to the Saudi Pro League club.

The side sits third in the league standings, but were humbled in the 3-1 loss to their fourth-placed rivals on the road.

Mane was not named in the matchday squad despite registering two assists in the club's last outing, a 6-2 victory against Asian Champions League opponents Pakhtakor FC.

One Saudi journalist is believed to have used Mane's absence to suggest that he was not sufficiently engaged with Al-Nassr's campaign this season.

But even the suggestion was enough to incense the former Tottenham head coach, who immediately asked if the journalist was 'a father?'

'Do you have children?' he queried, with the journalist responding that he did not.

Ange Postecoglou snapped at the journalist who questioned the strength of Sadio Mane's commitment to Al-Nassr

Should footballers ever be criticised for choosing family over club commitments?

The Senegal forward missed the match as he and his wife await the birth of their second child

'That's probably why you ask the question,' Postecoglou hit back. 'Because when you do, you'll realise it's the most important thing, the biggest blessing you can have.

'(Mane) is with his wife while she is having a baby, OK? Nothing is more important in life.

'Yes, he had my permission, my blessing, and Sadio Mane is one of the best people in this world, mate.

'Never question him or his commitment to this football club.'

Mane welcomed his first child with wife Aisha Timba last year, after marrying the then-18-year-old in January 2024.

In his first match following the happy news, Mane scored and celebrated by rocking an imaginary baby in his arms.

Postecoglou and Mane have only worked with one another since the beginning of the season, but appear to have formed a strong bond with Mane a frequent starter in the Riyadh-based starting XI.

The Antipodean manager joined the club following a spell without work after his ignominious departure from Nottingham Forest last season.

Since arriving in the Gulf state, Postecoglou has overseen a strong domestic campaign, with Al-Nassr registering just one previous defeat this season, against Al-Ettifaq.

But Friday's loss may have stung all the more after Al-Nassr initially led against their bitter rivals.

Cristiano Ronaldo had opened the scoring for the visitors on Friday evening in Jeddah, but missed a penalty striking the far post and failed to double his side's lead.

Instead, it was Ivan Toney who was nerveless from the spot as he netted to put Al-Ahli 2-1 up in the 71st minute, with Roger Ibanez providing the winner four minutes later.

Welcome to another Arsecast Extra, the Arsenal podcast, with myself and James from @gunnerblog.

#1547. Dortmund a tricky test + Guimaraes on getting to grips with Arteta’s midfield

Arsenal are in Champions League action this evening, taking on Borussia Dortmund at home. It’s a game that Kepa Arrizabalaga will start in the absence of David Raya, but the news around the Arsenal number 1 was a little more positive than expected. In his press conference yesterday, Mikel Arteta said:

He’s not fit for tomorrow, unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were all quite worried, but he seems to be better than what we expected.

We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at that moment, and the first test that we’ve done showed something that is much more encouraging. There’s no need for surgery, which was the main fear especially because that would rule him out for months, so let’s see.

So, it seems like he’s going to miss a few games, but not anything prolonged, which is obviously good news. Elsewhere, there’s room for rotation, and I think this might be a good chance to give minutes to William Saliba who hasn’t played competitively since the World Cup.  He’s had a couple of behind closed doors appearances, which will be useful in terms of fitness, but nothing compares with actually playing at this level.

I wonder too if players like Ben White, Cristhian Mosquera and Piero Hincapie will fancy their chances, but that seems like a lot of change in the back four – and the goalkeeper – so we’ll have to wait and see there. In midfield, we can bring Myles Lewis-Skelly in for a start, but obviously the manager has plenty to choose from in there, and up front I imagine it will be a chance for Viktor Gyokeres whose minutes have been scant so far this season. Asked if the striker had been knocking on his door about that, Arteta said:

No, we have conversations with every player to make sure that they understand what we are doing, to gather information about the way they are feeling, and so far, it’s been very positive with Viktor and with the rest of the team.

He could really use a goal tonight if he does start, as does Christos Tzolis whose numbers so far this season aren’t where you’d like them to be. Obviously there’s more to assessing a player than simply goals and assists, but for a left winger brought into replace two players who contributed a lot to the team over the last few seasons, just two assists from 11 appearances (Community Shield excluded) is a little below what you’d hope. He has had an injury, of course, but if his season needs a kick-start, tonight would be very timely.

Dortmund sit top of the Bundesliga right now, unbeaten in the league thus far, and with just one defeat all season in all competitions. That did come in the Champions League, away to Bodo Glimt, but this will be a tricky test tonight for Arsenal. Arteta says:

I’m very impressed with them, you see the results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga at the top and where they are in the Champions League and especially the way they are playing, the way they are dominating games, the amount of threat they are able to create. We had them here in pre-season, and they showed the quality and what they are capable of, so we are very much aware of that. But we play at home in front of our crowd, and now we’re going to go and attack the game, that’s for sure.

After a disappointing second half against Newcastle on Saturday, I’m sure the manager will be looking for a response from his side. It’s nice to be at home again, and a long spell of games in London will hopefully less taxing physically without all the travel, so it’d be good to get that off to a winning start tonight.

Elsewhere, Bruno Guimaraes spoke about his first few months at the club, and how he now feels like he’s getting to grips with what Mikel Arteta wants from him, saying:

I’m here, I don’t know, three, four months? It’s still a lot to go, but I now definitely understand my role in the team, the way that Mikel wants me to play in the team. So, yeah, I think I still can play much, much better.

And it’s quite interesting to hear him talk about how at Arsenal he is more ‘free’ than he was under Eddie Howe at Newcastle. Most would feel it was the other way around, but he explained:

It’s very different. When I was at Newcastle, you play more positional, keep more your position. Here it’s a little bit more free.

If you see the game against Newcastle, they were marking us man to man. You see JT [Jurrien Timber] plays a six, an eight and a number nine sometimes, so you have to move a lot. Of course, I was not used to it. So now I understand a little bit more what he wants for the midfield.

I think there’s more to come from him, he’s looked good at times, a little off the pace at others, and I think my main worry is about the physical side of his game. Does he have the running power and athleticism that enables players like Declan Rice and Martin Odegaard to thrive under this manager? At 29, he’s no spring chicken, but I guess there’s always room for improvement. Anyway, his press conference stuff from yesterday is worth reading, and there’s some good chat about him on the Arsecast Extra which you’ll find below.

Right, I’ll leave it there for this morning. At just 17, Mohya is already a versatile asset comfortable playing in several positions, and Ward will no doubt be watching on closely as the situation continues to develop.

#1544. Five Man United players who could leave in January as part of major Mauricio Pochettino clear-out

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 14:30, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:32

Manchester United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, with the club potentially making three mid-season signings.

The Red Devils currently find themselves down in 19th spot in the Premier League table and facing what would be a stunning relegation from the top flight.

There could also be first-team departures in the winter market, as new head coach Mauricio Pochettino begins to shape the squad.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five players who could potentially leave Old Trafford when the January market opens for business.

Zirkzee was linked with a move away from Man United over the summer, but he was ultimately not allowed to depart due to the fact that the Red Devils were unable to sign a replacement.

Even with Benjamin Sesko out injured, Zirkzee has not started a single match this season, with each of his 11 appearances coming off the bench.

The Netherlands international has scored twice this season, but his overall record for Man United since arriving from Bologna in 2024 is 11 goals in 86 appearances.

It has been a struggle for the 25-year-old in English football, but he is not short of interest, and a return to Serie A in January is seen as a serious possibility at this stage.

Como and Napoli are the latest clubs to be linked with Zirkzee.

Mazraoui is reportedly attracting the attention of AC Milan ahead of the January market, with a mid-season departure for the Morocco international thought to be possible.

The 29-year-old has underperformed in his nine appearances for Man United this season and is not believed to be in the club's long-term plans.

Initially, the defender impressed after arriving from Bayern Munich, and he has now represented the Red Devils on 86 occasions in all competitions.

However, a switch in the January market could be on the cards, especially if Man United are able to boost their options at full-back in the winter window.

Heaven is reportedly open to the idea of leaving Man United during the winter market.

The 20-year-old has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool in the team's last match, which ended in a 4-0 defeat.

Man United are expected to bring in a new centre-back in January, and Heaven is said to be concerned over what that would mean for his playing time.

As a result, the Englishman is allegedly open to a winter loan move, while a permanent exit is not being ruled out depending on what offers arrive.

Heaven, who has a contract with Man United until the summer of 2029, has made 32 appearances for the club since arriving from Arsenal in February 2025.

Martinez's contract with Man United is due to expire at the end of the campaign, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough season for the Argentine.

A new deal for the 28-year-old is seen as highly unlikely given that he has openly criticised Man United chiefs, such as director of football Jason Wilcox, during the 2026-27 season.

Man United will be reluctant to lose the Argentina international on a free transfer, so it is possible that a sale in the January window could occur, depending on the offer.

Martinez has been one of the team's biggest under-performers this season, and it appears that his time at Old Trafford will come to an end at some stage in 2027.

Amass may yet be given the chance to prove himself to new Man United head coach Pochettino, but the defender's future looks to be away from Old Trafford.

The 19-year-old was heavily linked with a departure during the summer window, but he stayed at Man United past the deadline and has made two appearances this season, both in the Champions League.

Amass was not in the squad against Liverpool last time out, though, and Luke Shaw's return to fitness has pushed him further down the pecking order.

A number of Championship clubs are believed to be keen on the teenager, who only has a deal with the 20-time English champions until the end of the season.

#1543. Why Liverpool have a point to prove against Man United: Andoni Iraola's side must end rotten run against 'Big Six' rivals - and Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak have to finally step up when it matters

Published: 01:42 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:02 EST, 23 November 2026

Given the carousel of chaos and never-ending crises at Old Trafford, it is easy to forget there are football storylines away from the headline-generating machine of Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino.

Lo and behold, there is – and Liverpool also enter Sunday’s clash against the old enemy with a point to prove.

One problem for Andoni Iraola is his side's frailties in the bigger games, which comes into focus this weekend with United in town – despite the desire to make an easy joke about how this is a clash against relegation fodder.

Since thrashing United 7-0 in 2023, Liverpool have beaten their friends in Manchester just once in seven meetings, including two draws and a defeat at Anfield.

To use a cliche, form seems to go out of the window for this fixture. In the last two Anfield meetings, Liverpool have been first and second in the table, United 14th and then tenth. This weekend, it is fourth against 18th, though Pochettino’s side could be bottom by kick-off.

Liverpool’s struggles in bigger games stretch further. Against the so-called 'Big Six’, the Reds have won just two of 12 games since winning the Premier League title. In a ‘mini league’ of those six sides, Liverpool are bottom in the aforementioned period.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side must prove on Sunday they can deliver in the biggest matches

Manchester United did the double over Liverpool in the Premier League last season

United did the double over Liverpool last season, Manchester City have beaten them four times in little over 12 months, Arsenal won on Merseyside a month ago.

So why has this team gone from looking formidable 18 months ago to rather flappable whenever the historic big boys are in town? Casual neutrals who only tune in for the showpiece Sunday 4.30pm may joke that they have not seen Liverpool play well for a good year.

A lot of the answer to that question comes back to Arne Slot and the issues we documented every week last season, when his side were dull and boring to watch, naked in defence and would capitulate in an instant.

Maybe players like Isak, Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola thrive more in intricate spaces rather than the gaping gaps left behind by the attack-minded bigger teams.

Another reason could be the simple fact that these sides are more likely to expose Liverpool’s vulnerabilities, such as the lack of a true defensive midfielder, the poor full backs or the frailties at defending set-pieces.

Anfield has lost its fear factor somewhat, too. Liverpool are top of the Premier League away table with 13 points from 15, but 18th in the home table with just one win in five games.

City had not won in front of a crowd there since 2003, now they have done it two seasons running. Arsenal had not triumphed at the stadium for 14 years until last month.

Iraola is aware of all this and said on Friday: ‘United finished third in the table last season. You are looking at a squad with exactly the same players. They had very, very good results, especially in the second half of the season.

Liverpool bemoaned Ryan Gravenberch’s red card in their home defeat to Manchester City

The Reds spurned a number of chances when they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal last month

‘Now we have just started, this is just 10 games. So, for sure, they will be a lot higher in the table (soon). We have to rate them like this and the truth is the reference we have is that they finished third.

‘We have to look at ourselves because we need the points. We need to improve our home form. It is also a big game in terms of relevance. It’s Liverpool v Manchester United, so we want to play well and we want to win.’

Asked if he understands the importance of the fixture to fans, Iraola – who spent the weekend off taking in grassroots football and netball games following his kids – said: ‘I am very aware! This is the biggest one in English football. In this country, this is the one.’

In Iraola’s first two bigger games, a theme threatened to emerge. Against Manchester City, Liverpool were well in the contest until Ryan Gravenberch’s red card but were toothless when it came to putting their chances away, lacking bite in attack.

The game was there to be won at 0-0, with the Anfield crowd roaring, but the Reds did not have the killer instinct to do so.

Against Arsenal, there were plenty of chances to equalise after the Gunners’ early goal but, again, goalkeeper David Raya could have put his feet up and had a cigar. A lot of territory but nothing to make the defence seriously sweat.

In both cases, Liverpool were on the receiving end of refereeing howlers. Gravenberch’s red was not a red – the first yellow should never be a booking – and Alexander Isak had a stonewall penalty turned down. ProRef has admitted errors.

To take a cynical view, though: in the title-winning campaign, we were rarely sat talking about referees or moaning about narrow misses or unfair results. Liverpool found ways to win and had no excuses.

Liverpool need Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak to step up against the league's big boys

And that brings us nicely on to Sunday. It feels like the script has been written for weeks.

Indeed, after United lost 3-0 to Bournemouth and the score was read out to huge cheers at Anfield, Daily Mail Sport wrote: ‘Everyone is looking forward to United sacking Michael Carrick and then rocking up at Anfield to win 1-0 with their new manager in a few weeks.’

It always seems to happen and it feels like United get results against rivals Liverpool and City even when they have felt close to their lowest ebb.

But Liverpool and Iraola must not allow that to happen. There can be no excuses of ‘new manager bounce’, refereeing calls or fine margins come Sunday tea time.

Isak and Wirtz simply must step up. It feels harsh that the pair, Wirtz especially, are always in the spotlight but the £125million and £116million signings have flattered to deceive against the big boys.

Both have been spectacular at times this term but need to show up when it really matters, while £123million addition Barcola is still waiting for his first Premier League goal.

Iraola has history with United. As a player, his Athletic Club side beat Sir Alex Ferguson’s great side 5-3 over two legs in Europe.

‘I said at the time, it was one of the best wins of my career,’ he said. 'United, I remember, were champions of the Premier League, got to the Champions League final and lost to Barcelona the year before. We honestly played much better than them.’

Iraola has remained unbeaten against United into his managerial career, winning two and drawing four of his six meetings with them.

Overall, the former Bournemouth boss has played 38 games against ‘Big Six’ teams in the league: winning ten, drawing ten, losing 18.

But a win is all that matters on Sunday and it is a chance for Liverpool to set the tempo ahead of a busy festive schedule. After already taking on the current top three, Iraola now contests two rivalries with a trip across the city to Everton next week.

Six of nine pre-Christmas games are at Anfield so there is a real chance to build a head of steam in the league, qualify for the next stage of Europe and get to the Carabao Cup semi-final.

Iraola would welcome those festive gifts but, for Liverpool fans, nothing will be sweeter than giving their old foes a good old walloping on Sunday.

#1541. Arsenal 1-1 Dortmund: Familiar flaws hold Arsenal back

A 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday raised some very familiar concerns and, if we’re being honest, revealed nothing we didn’t already know.

Arsenal can play world-class football and completely dominate teams for long spells, but lack the world-class attack to make the most of that domination, the sort of players you just know will create and convert big chances when the time comes. And the way the team is starting games after the break is worrying, with teams who are battered to within an inch of their lives early on suddenly able to compete.

I really feel like I could write two versions of today’s blog. One where I’m miserable, of course: the players can’t shoot, they make all the wrong choices in the decisive moment, we can’t keep wasting chances and dropping off after the break, if Andrea Berta doesn’t deliver the true heirs to Thierry Henry and Robert Pires in January, then he should be stuffed into one of the cannons outside the Armoury and fired into the cold night air.

The other version is much more glass half full: Arteta is coaching masterclasses every week, this level of dominance in games is something I could only dream of a few years ago, that’s the most shots we’ve had in a game all season, we’re top of the league, we’re creating loads without any set-piece reliance and without Bukayo Saka – the goals will come.

Some people reading this would prefer (and relate better to) one version, and others the other version, I’m sure. Let’s see where we end up!

There were, as there tends to be in these Champions League games, a fair few changes from the weekend. Kepa, Piero Hincapie, Ben White, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Christos Tzolis, and Viktor Gyokeres all came into the team.

Despite featuring half a different side, there were plenty of parallels with the Newcastle match. Arsenal were dominant from the off, with Hincapie and White taking turns to play off of Gyokeres. Dortmund had no idea how to cover them and both fullbacks were the targets of early crosses into the box.

After a couple of long-range efforts, Arsenal got their goal they deserved, with Gyokeres launching a ferocious, dipping effort beyond Gregor Kobel. The Swede can put his foot through the ball, that’s for sure, and the Dortmund backline gave him the sort of time and space to set himself that he doesn’t often get.

The pressure continued after the opener for a while, with Tzolis forcing a good save and Madueke just unable to sort his feet to tap in the rebound.

It’s fair to say the game settled down after 15/20 minutes, with Dortmund growing into it a little, but it was still Arsenal who looked like scoring the next goal. Rice shot over from almost the same patch of grass Gyokeres had scored from, and the midfielder had another chance when a beautiful one-touch move ended with him bursting through, hurtling towards the Dortmund box. Maybe he could’ve picked out Madueke in support, but he went alone and Nico Schlotterbeck just got across to block the shot.

Another huge chance was denied by the offside flag as much as the finishing – Madueke won the ball high, Odegaard squared it to Gyokeres, and the Swede fired over from near the penalty spot. Odegaard was ruled offside but I’m not convinced: had the ball hit the net, I think we’d have seen a very tight VAR check.

There was one thought on everyone’s minds at half-time: don’t do the same thing again. After Slavia Prague and Newcastle, do not do the same thing again.

Gyokeres was, by UEFA standards, lucky not to concede a penalty when a corner struck him on the arm. There was another early warning sign with Dortmund sliding the ball across the box and Maximilian Beier kicking the air. He didn’t make the same mistake with his next opportunity. Centre-back Joane Gadou (who was very impressive all evening) charged through the heart of the pitch before playing the ball to Beier, who jinked to unbalance Gabriel and slotted home.

Sometimes a goal is just a good goal, and I don’t think anyone was really at fault here. It’s a great run from Gadou, Beier tricks Gabriel to take the ball onto his weaker left side – it’s fair if Gabriel is expecting (and blocking the angle) on the attacker’s favoured foot, I know how that can happen. I think if we score that goal we’re talking about two brilliant individuals, rather than defensive errors.

My first thought? Not again. My second? OK, how do we respond? Because on Saturday, the response was poor.

This time it was a lot better. Jobe Bellingham had a rebound disallowed for offside, a moment that really brought the crowd back into the game, but in truth, that was Dortmund’s only real moment of threat. From the goal on 55 minutes to full-time, Arsenal had 15 shots to Dortmund’s two.

And that doesn’t include Serhou Guirassy playing one-twos with the post after a clever, low free-kick from Martin Odegaard late on.

Madueke had an effort blocked. Gyokeres flicked a header wide. Madueke shot wide beyond the far post after a good run. Gyokeres missed a big chance with his head from six yards out. Rice hit the near post from a tight angle after a brilliant pass from Eberechi Eze.

A couple of late corners came to nothing, and that was it.

Mikel Arteta was clearly pleased with the performance on the whole:

Well, I think I love the way the team played. There’s no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game … It was great to watch. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn’t ended up in the back of the net. That’s my feeling.

to do what we’ve done out there is just something to be very, very pleased about, because there is very little more that we can demand from the team.

But we all know what that little more is:

obviously the feeling is that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, the amount of chances, the situation, and even shots that are not there. We are three against two, two against one, and the ball doesn’t land with the right person. There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.

Often when Arsenal don’t win games, it feels like it’s because the team haven’t created enough chances. We end up focusing on that one moment, where that one player didn’t execute the way you wanted. But last night wasn’t one of those: Arsenal didn’t struggle to turn dominance into good, slick football, and that football into a healthy number of decent opportunities.

That’s incredibly frustrating, but I do think you win a lot more often than not when you do that. Maybe that’s a hard sell for some this morning, but it’s how I feel about it when we play well, especially when we’ve been winning games anyway. That’s the first time this season we’ve gone two without a win across all competitions, and we’ve won 14 of 19 games so far. Sometimes things don’t fall for you, and this one felt a lot like ‘one of those’, certainly more than Newcastle did.

A word for a couple of promising performances too, with the boss asked about Gyokeres in his post-match press conference:

What I love the most is how connected he was to the team. We used him many times in different ways. His link-up play, the way he held the ball, the way he threw it in behind and stretched the pitch. There was a lot to like in that performance and that’s the victory that we need.

His finishing was off after the brilliant opener, but at least he was in the positions: too often this season and last, Gyokeres has gone through a game barely registering a shot. He had seven last night, and if he can do that more often he’ll score a lot more. His general play was improved too, both holding the ball up and competing in behind.

And I thought Martin Odegaard was excellent too. His eight chances created from open play was the most of any player in any Champions League match so far this season.

Since we returned to the competition in 2023, we’ve had a player create more than five chances in a match just twice: Odegaard at Napoli in September (6) and Odegaard last night (9). He’s incredibly unlucky not to be leaving the game with a couple of assists.

The draw leaves us in a decent position to finish in the all-important top eight in the league phase still, although you have to squint a bit to see us landing in the also-important top two. Real Madrid are up next and that’s a reminder of the sort of teams we’re up against: finishing in the top two is a tall order at the best of times.

With each passing game, it is impossible not to wonder what could be done in January to add to the team. Unless there’s a sudden uptick out of nowhere, those thoughts aren’t disappearing. And even if there is a massive uptick, those thoughts will still be around. But 30 shots is the most we’ve had in a game all season, and the same group of players have scored more goals with fewer shots (/chances) plenty of times. Let’s hope we see some more clinical finishing on Sunday.

Guess I landed on the glass half full version.

There should be an Arsecast once Blogs has caught up with the game, so stay tuned for that. Enjoy your Wednesdays!

#1540. Opinion: Liverpool find surprise solution to midfield problems

Liverpool's midfield has been a major topic of conversation for a while now.

Ever since Fabinho left in 2023, fans have demanded that new players were brought in by the Anfield outfit.

Obviously, that still hasn't happened with Arne Slot and Andoni Iraola actually making Liverpool's midfield weaker thanks to their sales of Tyler Morton and Curtis Jones over the last couple of seasons.

In the summer, most fans thought that at least one midfielder would be brought in to replace Jones but, instead, Trey Nyoni was given a more prominent role.

And, while he's done well this term, since he's still so young, he can't be playing two 90 minute games every week which is why a new midfielder now needs to be brought in.

Gavi could be Liverpool's surprise solution to their problems

Over the last few years, many different players have been discussed as potential options for Liverpool to explore.

Recently, Lamine Camara, Adam Wharton and Alex Scott have been the most linked with an Anfield switch.

However, in the upcoming January transfer window, each of them will only be available for crazy high fees.

And, with how many clubs have shown an interest in acquiring their services, there's going to be a huge battle for every single player.

That's why this latest update from journalist Juan Jesus is exciting.

"In addition to Alejandro Balde, Barça are now pushing Gavi out this very winter to fund the signing of a centre-back, seen as the club’s absolute priority," he wrote.

"The main target to bolster the defence is Nico Schlotterbeck, but the current wage bill leaves no room to pull off a move of that magnitude in January.

"To comply with financial fair play rules and try to sign him in this winter window, the board is pushing for two key sales: Balde on one hand, and the bombshell departure of Gavi on the other."

At the start of the 2026-27 season, nobody thought that Gavi would become available on the market.

He's been a regular feature in Flick's plans for as long as anyone can remember and, since he's only 22 years old, there's so much of his career left to go.

Obviously, a deal wouldn't come cheap for the Spaniard but, if the La Liga giants are as strapped for cash as they seem to be, an agreement could probably be reached.

Gavi can also play as a number 10, eight or six which is massively beneficial for the Reds.

This versatility coupled with his endless experience of the Champions League and La Liga all join together to make him the perfect player for Liverpool to sign.

Here's hoping that an agreement can be reached.

#1539. Real Salt Lake vs Vancouver Whitecaps - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:36

Real Salt Lake will try to extend their season into next week with a Friday win over the Vancouver Whitecaps at America First Field in game two of that best-of-three playoff series.

The reigning MLS Cup runners-up captured game one 2-0 last Sunday, putting them one win away from round two in the Western Conference playoffs.

After surviving a nervy shootout in the Wild Card Round, Salt Lake are now on the brink of elimination yet again after a subpar showing in game one against the Caps.

On Sunday, Pablo Mastroeni’s men suffered just their second defeat in their last eight MLS outings and were second-best for much of the game.

While they are on the verge of another early exit, they can draw optimism from being unbeaten in their last four MLS affairs at America First Field.

During the regular season, Salt Lake showed strong attacking potency on home soil, netting three or more goals six times and scoring multiple times on 12 separate occasions.

They will try to end a five-match playoff losing run on Friday, scoring a goal or fewer in each of those instances.

Claret and Cobalt have not lost a playoff match at home in 90 minutes this decade, with their only such victory at America First Field occurring on penalties versus the Houston Dynamo in game two of that opening round series.

It is just one game, but Vancouver looked very much like title contenders as they began the 2026 MLS post-season in style.

Jesper Sorensen’s side carried the play throughout game one and will seek a fifth consecutive MLS triumph on Friday.

While this is the fourth straight year the Caps are in the post-season, they have won only once in that span in normal time away from home, beating San Diego 3-1 in the Western Conference Final last year.

Meanwhile, they failed to win three of their final four regular-season away fixtures this season against Western Conference opposition, with the highest-scoring team in the West failing to score on two of those occasions.

Vancouver have never lost a playoff encounter under Sorensen when netting first but have also never won a post-season outing in 90 minutes when conceding the opener under his leadership.

Sorensen, meanwhile, has won every match against RSL as the Caps boss, including their last two visits to America First Field, in which his team scored three goals both times.

Vancouver Whitecaps Major League Soccer form:

Due to a hamstring strain, Ariath Piol may miss this match for RSL, while Diego Luna and Emeka Eneli are questionable because of knee injuries and Zach Booth still has to clear concussion protocol.

Sergi Solans has scored three goals in his last two MLS home outings, including the opener in their 2-1 win over the Los Angeles Galaxy on Decision Day, while Rafael Cabral kept game one close, making six saves, many of them spectacular.

On the Vancouver side, an illness may keep Belal Halbouni out on Friday, and it is unlikely we will see Kenji Cabrera feature as he deals with a foot injury.

Edier Ocampo got the Caps on the board late in the opening half of game one, with Bruno Caicedo adding some insurance in the final 45 minutes.

Cabral; Yedlin, Glad, Quinton, Engel, Sanabria; Lobjanidze, Guske, Spierings, Guilavogui; Solans

Vancouver Whitecaps possible starting lineup:

Takaoka; Ocampo, Blackmon, Priso, Johnson; Larraz, Cubas; Sabbi, Muller, Caicedo; White

The Caps have far too many weapons for RSL to contend with, and even a heroic Cabral between the sticks might not be enough to fend off the visitors given their current form.

#1538. Liverpool's win over Man United was a landmark day for Andoni Iraola - he is playing a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of, writes LEWIS STEELE

Published: 02:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 05:29 EST, 23 November 2026

A Liverpool manager wearing a toothy grin and black puffer jacket as he lapped up the adulation of Anfield with three fist bumps in front of the Kop… where have we seen that before?

Andoni Iraola may not look as natural at the grand gestures or possess the aura of his predecessor Jurgen Klopp just yet – but this still felt like a landmark day for the Basque manager.

Playing a heavy-metal style of football that Klopp would be proud of, Iraola has impressed in his early months at Liverpool but craved a real scalp against a rival to turbocharge the feeling among the fanbase and give his tenure true lift-off.

This was the finest day of the fledgling new era as Iraola’s relentless Reds were unstoppable and humiliated their biggest rivals – and the boss must be rubbing his hands at his depth of attacking weapons.

Rio Ngumoha, unbelievably still just 18, was the pick of the bunch and United simply could not get near him, while Florian Wirtz put in his best performance in a Reds shirt and Dominik Szoboszlai looked back to his breathtaking best.

Szoboszlai started the rout with a devastating free-kick and swung an imaginary golf club in celebration, then pretended to watch his tee shot fly into the Anfield Road Stand.

Andoni Iraola is playign a style of football that Jurgen Klopp would be proud of at Liverpool

Sticking on the Hungarian’s theme, the gulf in quality between these two teams felt like that of a professional golfer compared to a rookie who can barely get the ball off the driving range.

Szoboszlai got his driver out to score a thumping strike and continue his role as the Premier League’s best dead-ball specialist – and Liverpool never looked back from there.

All the talk centred around Mauricio Pochettino’s soft side and the embarrassing sequence of events that led to Lenny Yoro’s early red card but let’s take nothing away from Liverpool, who were breathtaking and unstoppable.

The fact the score was only 4-0 flattered United. To be picky and find criticism in feedback of Liverpool, they were wasteful. This could have been five, six, seven, you name it.

Ngumoha was unplayable. The England international was only four when United won the last of their league titles and Sir Alex Ferguson departed, so he will not remember this team being competent. But the teenager knew the significance of his performance in this fixture.

His assist for Florian Wirtz was eye-catching, his goal to make it 3-0 deserved after a lung-busting run off the ball. Poor Diogo Dalot will have nightmares for days about Ngumoha’s dancing feet as the Liverpool winger skipped past him time and again.

There were times when Ngumoha played the wrong pass which is the most frightening thing for rivals. This kid is far from the finished product. He will only get better and can be one of the best forwards in the game in a year or so.

He is level-headed unlike some other egotistical young stars and he plays with a smile on his face. Why wouldn’t he?

Rio Ngumoha was unplayable against Manchester United at Anfield and will only get better

Liverpool will pay a maximum of £6.8million for him, based on add-ons after poaching him from Chelsea two years ago. In the week of Grand Theft Auto IV’s release, the heist of Ngumoha feels like the grandest theft of all (though he is only just old enough to play the video game!).

Those around him are all £100million signings but his ceiling is just as high as that of Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

It helps that all four clicked in this game. Wirtz has been excellent this season but has not performed in the bigger fixtures. Conversations after losses to Manchester City and Arsenal centred around Wirtz not showing up.

The German was everywhere here and United were left to chase shadows. It is not an exaggeration to label this his best Liverpool performance, with an easy-on-the-eye goal and some moments of creative genius.

Barcola destroyed United with his pace, Szoboszlai was a constant menace, while Isak did everything right until it came to finishing several attacks.

And that is the thing that will excite the head coach and should leave rival fans quaking in their boots. This team is full of virtuoso match-winners but all of them have plenty of room to improve. If they do that and all fulfil their potential, the sky is the limit for Iraola’s Liverpool.

Liverpool have already been linked with a lot of players this season.

Whether he's used as a number 10, a right winger or a striker, Liverpool would have an incredible player on their hands if they manage to get a deal over the line.

Here's hoping they do and the Reds add even more firepower to their already stacked attack.

#1534. Why Andoni Iraola - NOT Jurgen Klopp - deserves credit for fixing Florian Wirtz, Omar Berrada's Sky appearance has made things worse for Man United and is Cole Palmer at the wrong club? IAN LADYMAN on MY FOOTBALL WEEKEND

Published: 07:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 09:00 EST, 23 November 2026

In what transpired to be a lively Sky TV studio at Anfield, Daniel Sturridge turned in one of his own performances of the season.

The former Chelsea and Liverpool striker is proving himself a pundit of real substance and he cut to the heart of one of the more ridiculous notions of the week, namely that a week away with Jurgen Klopp had solved all Florian Wirtz’s problems at a stroke.

‘I think we should give credit to Andoni Iraola,’ he said as we all breathed a sigh at the sound of some common sense.

The obsession with Klopp among many people who support and follow Liverpool remains terrifyingly real and the former Anfield manager plays to it.

But to suggest – as many who should know better have done – that Klopp managed to fix Wirtz in four sessions last week is as lazy and ridiculous as it is utterly disrespectful to current Liverpool manager Iraola.

Wirtz had a good couple of games with his national team, for sure. He scored three goals which will have done much for confidence. He was fabulous against Manchester United's ten men.

Florian Wirtz has found his form at just the right time for Liverpool

Reds boss Andoni Iraola deserves credit for the German's transformation this season

But anybody who has watched even a small portion of Liverpool’s game this season will have seen a player gradually growing in stature and finally, it seems, adjusting to the largely unique rhythms of the Premier League.

Iraola is a talented coach. Talk to players and staff at Bournemouth and they will tell you that. He improves footballers and steadily he is bringing his influence to bear on Wirtz.

The 23-year-old still has some way to go. He can still look half a yard too slow on occasion. But he has created 29 Liverpool chances from open play this season.

It tends to be the execs rather than the managers who get the blame at United but Mauricio Pochettino sadly had his fingerprints on what happened on Merseyside.

He was right to complain about the sending off of Leny Yoro. Alexander Isak was never getting the ball and referee Sam Barrott should have given himself time to consider that before getting the red card out.

In those situations the defender should be given the benefit of any doubt.

The decision has an enormous impact on the game, something that seemed to pass many people by.

Nevertheless the passage of play had at its inception a horror moment from Matthijs de Ligt that most of us could have seen coming the moment the team sheet dropped.

Sometimes it doesn’t pay for a manager to try and be the smartest bloke in the room.

Mauricio Pochettino should shoulder some of the blame for United's dismal defeat at Anfield

BERRADA INTERVENTION NOT USEFUL FOR UNITED

No doubt the decision to plonk Omar Berrada in front of a TV camera was driven by good intentions by United.

The club’s executives had been accused of hiding while Old Trafford burned so here was one of them, sitting smartly in front of a huge club crest, ready to tell the world that everything would be OK.

The only problem is that the words of Berrada, United’s chief executive, have arguably made things worse.

Berrada didn’t catch much of a break over the weekend.

Just 48 hours after telling the world that United were happy with their ‘nine defenders’  Pochettino’s team were given such a chasing at Anfield that one wondered if the new manager may be tempted to chuck all of them on at the same time.

None of this is about luck, however. Neither good nor bad. It’s about planning and the lack thereof.

Liverpool, remember, also had a big defensive problem over the summer.

Omar Berrada's surprise appearance on Sky Sports has made things worse for Man United

The two full-backs bought in the summer of 2025 – Jeremie Frimpong and Milos Kerkez – had struggled while another – Conor Bradley – was injured. In the centre, Ibrahima Konate had left for Real Madrid while young prospect Giovanni Leoni had not played since suffering a dreadful knee injury on his debut last year.

That left Virgil Van Dijk, Jeremy Jacquet and Joe Gomez. Liverpool could have struggled on. They could have counted numbers and hoped. They could have prayed for better form and fitness from the defenders they had.

But that would have been unfair on incoming manager Iraola. So in mid-August they took the Uruguayan international Ronald Araujo on loan from Barcelona and it has transpired to be a signing utterly fundamental to Liverpool’s season so far.

There was little fuss and fanfare about the deal. All the noise was reserved for the £125million winger Bradley Barcola.

But Araujo – signed as a centre-half – is a former Barcelona captain and has solved Liverpool’s right-back problem at a stroke. He was as unfussy and effective against United yesterday as he has been all season.

This is how recruitment at big clubs works. They identify problems and use their data, imagination and contacts to solve them. They don’t count the number of bodies in the dressing room and then sit on their hands telling themselves it is enough.

Every United supporter in the land could have told Berrada and his friends that United needed defensive quality in the summer. But United thought they knew best and were wrong.

It is genuinely terrifying to think just what they may do next.

The second most productive footballer in terms of assists in the league is Brighton’s Pascal Gross but the German was left as bemused as anyone as his team somehow managed to lose a game they dominated at Hull.

Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler has said he wants his players to behave like a big team but perhaps some naivety let them down as Hull scored two in added time on Humberside.

The first of Ollie McBurnie’s goals came in the 92nd minute on the back of a quick counter and it was one that could have been stopped at source by what Pep Guardiola used to call a ‘technical foul’ – a trip or a nudge – before the ball had even crossed the halfway line.

Nobody wishes to encourage foul play but the truth is that Guardiola’s City would not have conceded that goal. Nor, for that matter, would Arsenal.

Brighton's naivety saw them suffer a surprise defeat by Hull City on Sunday

At the Etihad, Enzo Maresca gave Phil Foden a start ahead of Rayan Cherki and the City playmaker showed some glimpses of his fabulous talent.

Nevertheless the longer this period of uncertainty goes on for Foden, the harder it is to work out how it ends.

Maresca wants to play with two out and out wide players at City.

Jeremy Doku and Iliman Ndiaye started in the draw against Fulham while Antoine Semenyo will play when he is fit.

So with Cherki established as City’s creative hub just behind Haaland, Foden is on the fringes a little.

He signed a contract in June and is now tied to the club until 2030. Equally, Foden will be 27 next May and should be approaching his physical and creative peak.

Meanwhile Cole Palmer’s frustrations with life at Chelsea – highlighted in this column earlier this season – have now boiled over with a show of petulance at the end of his team’s Stamford Bridge hammering at the hands of Leeds.

The more this unfolds, the more it feels like Palmer is at the wrong club.

Palmer – for all that he tries to suggest otherwise – is an emotionally complex young athlete. He can be unpredictable and dramatic.

He needs calm around him, not persistent drift.

Cole Palmer's petulance at Stamford Bridge on Saturday has left us asking: Is he at the wrong club?

Another stunning result for Daniel Farke’s Leeds who now sit sixth in the table with the second best defensive record in the top flight.

Farke remains out of contract next summer and that still feels odd.

The club’s favourite media outlets told us last month that an ‘agreement had been reached in principle’ but still no white smoke from Elland Road.

Tottenham have crept into the top half for the first time this season after beating Ipswich with credit due to manager Roberto de Zerbi for handing teenager Luca Williams-Barnett his chance.

With big money summer signings Savio and Omar Marmoush sitting on the bench, Williams-Barnett scored the opening goal and became the fourth youngest player in history to score on his first Premier League start.

Of the three ahead of him in the list, Canadian Daniel Jebbison, now 23, currently sits on the Bournemouth bench, Danny Cadamarteri’s career became rather itinerant once he made the last of his 94 Everton league starts while Mark Cullen travelled from Hull to Bamber Bridge via outposts such as Luton, Blackpool, Port Vale, Hartlepool and Fylde.

Williams-Barnett will have enjoyed his weekend but history tells us the road ahead may not be straight.

Luca Williams-Barnett became the fourth youngest debut goalscorer in Premier League history

Of the new managers in this season’s top division, it has taken time for some to find their feet.

Iraola now has a statement Anfield win, for example, while at Bournemouth and Fulham Marco Rose and Alvaro Arbeloa no longer have to look at the league table through their fingers.

At Newcastle, it appears rather more complicated.

Eddie Howe’s replacement Matthias Jaissle doesn’t look chuffed with the players he was handed in the summer window but historical issues stalk him too.

Last season’s big money flop Yoane Wissa started this one well and looked ready to fly after starring and scoring in an August win at Spurs.

That was the £50million forward’s last goal, though, and he also only has one assist to his name.

On Saturday in the gutsy draw with Arsenal he came on in the 83rd minute and that spoke volumes.

One player whose career has headed the other way is Aston Villa defender Victor Lindelof.

The Swede was signed on a free from Manchester United largely to make the numbers up in August 2025 but his rise to prominence has been such that Match of the Day were moved to note his absence through injury from the team that drew with Sunderland at Villa Park.

Lindelof is 32 now but has just signed a new contract at Villa. Another one to benefit from Unai Emery’s regenerative elixir.

Unai Emery's coaching magic has helped transform the fortunes of Victor Lindelof

If this weekend has been – in part – about defenders then the Fulham recruitment staff deserve their props too.

The west London club had conceded seven goals in losing their opening three league games before Austrian defender David Affenbruger arrived on the last day of the summer window.

Debuting in the 0-0 draw at Liverpool that followed, Fulham have since lost just one of the seven subsequent games in which he has played.

The fee? £8.5million. Further proof that it really can be done.

#1532. Maritimo vs Nacional - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 25 Nov 2026 16:48

Maritimo and Nacional renew their Madeira derby rivalry in the Primeira Liga on Friday evening, with both sides looking to claim an important victory and move further clear of the drop zone.

The two clubs are meeting in the top flight for the first time in five years, with the visitors sitting 13th in the Primeira Liga table on 10 points from 11 matches, just two points above the 15th-placed hosts, who have a game in hand against Estoril Praia and sit outside the relegation playoff place on head-to-head points ahead of Casa Pia.

Maritimo made an encouraging start to life back in the top flight, winning their opening two league fixtures against Casa Pia and Famalicao, but they have not claimed another Primeira Liga victory since beating the latter on August 16.

Mitchell van der Gaag's side have since gone eight league matches without a win (D2, L6), including defeats in their last three such outings against Porto (2-1), Vitoria de Guimaraes (5-0) and Santa Clara (2-0).

Only bottom-placed Estoril, who are yet to win a league match this season, have endured a longer winless run, while Maritimo have scored the third-fewest goals in the division (nine) and conceded the third-most (21).

Van der Gaag's men have also struggled to make home advantage count, recording just one victory from five league matches at their own ground and losing the last three, during which they conceded multiple goals on each occasion and scored just once.

Maritimo did, however, receive a welcome boost in the Taca de Portugal last weekend, progressing past Chaves following a goalless draw and a 3-2 penalty shootout victory, and will hope that result provides some momentum ahead of Friday's derby.

Nacional have also endured a difficult start to the campaign, but they have collected six points from their last three matches, including a 1-0 victory over Academico de Viseu courtesy of Matchoi Djalo's late winner.

That result marked the first victory under new boss Joao Henriques, who arrived in late October as the club's third permanent manager of the season following the departures of Joao Giao and Alexandre Santos.

Henriques initially struggled to build on interim coach Bruno Abreu's home victory over Braga, losing away to Arouca in his first match in charge, but the latest success has given the Alvinegros an opportunity to record consecutive competitive wins for the first time since beating Alverca and Tondela in April.

Interestingly, Nacional's last four matches have each produced just one goal, including their disappointing Taca de Portugal defeat to lower-division Sanjoanense on October 17, meaning taking maximum points on Friday could hinge on greater efficiency in attack and defensive discipline.

However, the Islanders still have plenty of room for improvement away from home, having collected just one point from five Primeira Liga trips this season, drawing at Santa Clara on the opening weekend before losing their next four against Vitoria, Sporting, Rio Ave and Arouca.

Nacional have also found this fixture difficult in recent meetings, losing four of their last five league encounters with Maritimo across the Primeira Liga and Liga 2 (D1), including a 3-1 defeat on their most recent competitive visit.

Maritimo are monitoring defenders Rafael Fernandes (muscle) and Paulo Henrique (thigh), who both missed last weekend's cup tie against Chaves.

Yellu Santiago is also working his way back to full fitness from an injury, having only featured in the opening weekend of the Primeira Liga campaign.

Goncal Tabuaco's performance against Chaves has given Van der Gaag a decision to make in goal after he replaced Fran Vieites in the cup, saving two penalties during the shootout.

Nacional will be without Ulisses Wilson and Filipe Soares, who are both recovering from ankle injuries and remain unavailable.

Leo Santos (knee) is also sidelined, while Brazilian duo Wesley Gasolina and Liziero continue to recover from their respective injuries.

Henriques could retain the lineup that started against Viseu, with Miguel Baeza anchoring the midfield, although Djalo is pushing for a starting place after making an impact from the bench last time out.

Vieites; Igor Juliao, Correia, Szalai; Tavares, Andrade, Guzzo, Ogbeta; Bassouamina, Butzke Tejon

Marin; Jensen, Goncalves, Vitor, Kokolo; Baeza, Dias, Djalo; Labidi, Njoya, Song

Maritimo have struggled to turn home advantage into league points this season, but Nacional's poor away record gives the hosts reason to believe they can avoid defeat, making a share of the spoils a reasonable prediction.

#1529. Report: Bayern Munich preparing shock Liverpool double swoop

Liverpool are finally starting to find their feet under Andoni Iraola.
