#1496. Arsenal eye Serie A’s 11-goal striker: Should they pay £26m?

Arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested. The 21-year-old Portugal forward has scored 11 goals in 11 Serie A games since joining from Benfica B in July. Barcelona are equally keen, Inter watch him live at every match, and Napoli are reported as his strongest Italian suitor.

The interest makes sense. Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals. Arsenal’s results haven’t suffered, but their number nine position has produced little.

Finishing is the selling point. FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes. The weaknesses are just as clear: he wins 34% of his duels, completes 41% of his dribbles and ranks in the ninth percentile among forwards for defensive contribution, which clashes with the pressing Arteta wants from his striker.

Di Marzio says Monza will listen at around £22m to £26m, with the money earmarked for other signings, after paying about £3m including bonuses. Flashscore reports Benfica hold a 20% sell-on and a right to match offers, and Varela’s agents meet Monza this week.

Yes, but in the summer and only if Gyokeres leaves. Arsenal’s results are strong, so a January rush for a 21-year-old would add risk without fixing a crisis. A fee near £26m looks modest beside the £64m Gyokeres cost, and Varela’s goals-per-game record argues for the gamble far more than Gyokeres’ two in 15 does.

The real risk is suitability. He also scores for a struggling side, so his chances come in games unlike most of the Premier League games Arsenal play. Arteta needs a number nine who presses and wins duels, and Varela does neither well, so Arsenal would be buying a finisher and building the rest of his game themselves.

That is workable if Varela arrives as competition for Havertz rather than the first choice. Arsenal should also expect resistance beyond the price, because Benfica’s matching right and Inter’s summer plans complicate any early bid.

Watching him until June costs Arsenal nothing, and another 20 league games will show whether this form is real or a hot streak.

Tomorrow evening, AC Milan will entrust Ardon Jashari with the job of filling Luka Modric’s shoes, after the Croatian’s injury.

#1494. Ian Holloway SACKED by Swindon two days after trying to confront angry fans in feisty full-time scenes at Newport - with Premier League cult hero claiming club's training ground is haunted

Published: 05:52 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 10:57 EST, 23 November 2026

Ian Holloway has been sacked by Swindon just two days after attempting to confront angry fans following defeat to Newport on Saturday.

The journeyman manager had himself called the 2-0 loss on the road 'unforgivable' after he was taunted by home supporters chanting that he would be 'sacked in the morning' after the result.

Holloway had intended to go down the tunnel after the final whistle, and passed the away stand on his route out, taking off his cap as he held up his hands in resignation.

But as boos rained down on him, the 63-year-old could not resist the urge to engage, looking to answer back to the fans before he was restrained by security.

Last month, Holloway described himself as a 'dead man walking' with the Robins mired 17th in League Two, but Monday morning saw him despatched after two seasons in charge.

'Since joining the club towards the end of 2024, Ian has played an important role in stabilising our on-field position and helping the club make progress season upon season,' the Swindon statement announcing his departure read.

Saturdays eh.#STFC pic.twitter.com/1GL3blApwW

Ian Holloway was caught up in a clash with fans after Swindon's defeat to Newport County - shortly before he was sacked (Source: X/Loathed Stranger)

The journeyman manager oversaw two seasons at the club, saving them from relegation in 2024-25

'However, following careful consideration of recent results and performances, the club believes that now is the right time to take a different direction.

'This has not been an easy decision, but the board firmly believes that it is important to make difficult decisions when necessary, always with the best interests of Swindon Town at heart.'

Holloway cut a disillusioned figure at Rodney Parade as he gave a heartfelt assessment of his side's performance after defeat to the Exiles.

'It's devastating,' said Holloway. 'I'm bitterly disappointed. Did I expect my team to do that? Not in a million years.

'We're getting regular mistakes from almost everyone in that backline and in that midfield. We knew what type of game it was going to be. There's no excuses. I've just said to them "what on Earth do you think you're doing?" To start that way? It was so passive it was unforgivable.

'It's very painful at the minute. It'll come back at the manager in the end if I listen to all these people (from the stands).

'This is football. I've been in it a long time. This is my life.'

Holloway also questioned the desire of his players, continuing: 'Bitterly disappointed in all of them and disappointed for the fans. I get it, that didn't look like our team.

'They scored two ugly goals. All our chances that we had, normally we take them.

'Where's the fight? It's a local derby. I'm sorry, they've done their bits better than us.'

Holloway has endured an uneven stint at Swindon since 2024, saving the club from relegation in his first season but failing to challenge for the promotion places as time wore on.

Memorably, the former Crystal Palace and Queen's Park Rangers manager claimed that the training ground was haunted shortly after his arrival in Wiltshire.

Holloway had first suggested that there had been 'some strange things happening' after the club captain Ollie Clarke had ruptured his ankle in training, before enlisting his wife Kim to free spirits potentially trapped in the South West.

'I'm absolutely devastated so I'm going to try and cleanse the training ground area because people are telling me it's haunted,' Holloway said on BBC Radio Wiltshire in November 2024.

'There's a graveyard somewhere near. Honestly, I'm not joking.

'I think our training ground is very close to an ancient burial site so I'm going to get my wife to come up and say sorry to all these people and hopefully we'll have a bit more luck.'

Manchester United and Sporting Lisbon have confirmed their starting teams for Wednesday's Champions League contest in Portugal.

#1492. Bremer earns Juventus 2-2 draw at Fiorentina but leaves them six points off Champions League places

Gleison Bremer's equaliser earned Juventus a point at the Stadio Artemio Franchi after they twice fell behind against Fiorentina. Spalletti's side now go into the international break outside the Champions League places, with their next home game brought forward by a day.

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

The hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

The closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

At his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti said he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything important. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 8, 2026

The draw ended a run of two wins, against AZ Alkmaar and Napoli. Woltemade and Pellegrino both received a rating of 8.2 from the data provider.

#1491. Chelsea’s England playmaker on Man Utd’s radar

Chelsea transfer news around Cole Palmer has flared again, with Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival at Manchester United reviving the noise. Reporter Dean Jones insists the England playmaker’s future at Stamford Bridge is not in doubt, but he admits the sentiment around it is becoming harder to ignore.

Palmer, a boyhood United supporter, has been linked with Old Trafford before. United appointed Pochettino on 18 November after sacking Michael Carrick following one win in ten league games. The Argentine made Palmer one of his most used players at Chelsea, where the pair built a positive relationship, and Palmer scored 22 league goals in 2023/24.

Jones rates the chances of Palmer joining United as extremely low. United’s January budget stands at roughly £50m, and they want a left-back, a centre-back and a striker. A player FotMob values at €100m, roughly £87m, sits outside both the money and the shopping list. Jones also sees no sign that Palmer wants to leave, and says relations at Stamford Bridge would need to break down badly first.

Palmer has started all 11 of Chelsea’s Premier League games this season, playing 970 minutes for three goals, one from the penalty spot, and three assists. His 23 chances created include six big chances, and his 2.58 expected goals backs up the output. Xabi Alonso says, “The better Cole we have, the better Chelsea we have”.

Only ten of Palmer’s 31 shots have hit the target; he wins 46.9% of his dribbles, and he has collected two yellows and a red. Fitness worries more after an injury-hit 2025/26 that ended with him missing the World Cup.

No, but Chelsea should treat Jones’s condition as the real warning. Palmer’s contract runs to 2034, and United’s budget does not reach his valuation, so the danger lies in a deteriorating relationship, not a bid. That puts the onus on Alonso, Chelsea’s seventh permanent manager since 2021.

Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival from Aston Villa creates the obvious flashpoint. If Palmer feels crowded out of the number ten role, or pushed wide right too often, the homesickness talk will return. Clear roles and managed minutes will protect him better than another forward.

The money belongs elsewhere. Alonso’s side beat United 2-0 on 31 October, then lost 1-0 at Sunderland eight days later, and defensive brittleness and thin squad depth keep undermining a front line that already scores. A back line that leaks goals will not.

Liverpool transfer news from Goal says Ajax teenager Abdellah Ouazane is a January target as attacking cover for Florian Wirtz. Julian Ward, Liverpool’s recruitment chief, has reportedly sped up plans to support the £116m playmaker, and Ouazane has become a serious option before the winter window opens. Wael Mohya and Gilberto Mora sit on the same shortlist.

The 17-year-old grew up supporting Liverpool and badly wants to play at Anfield. Ajax hold the leverage, though: his contract runs to 2028, and persuading them to sell a prized academy graduate mid-season will take careful negotiation. De Telegraaf also reported earlier this season that sporting director Jordi Cruyff wants to give him a new deal when he turns 18 on 15 January.

Ouazane is mainly an attacking midfielder who also plays wide or up front. FotMob‘s 2026/27 numbers show two goals and one assist in 12 Eredivisie games, only four of them starts, across 441 minutes. His goals and shot attempts rank in the 88th and 86th percentiles among comparable attackers.

The gaps are just as clear: he sits in the 19th percentile for defensive contributions and the 15th for aerial duels won, and a 45.7% dribble success rate suggests he still loses the ball too often against senior opponents. Real Madrid pulled out of a 2025 deal after his medical, though Ajax’s own checks cleared him.

Iraola’s Liverpool press harder and play more direct than they did under Arne Slot, so that defensive profile matters. Wirtz works as the central creator with Bradley Barcola, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha out wide, which leaves the number 10 role as Ouazane’s only route in.

Yes, but as a planned investment rather than genuine cover. Wirtz missed several matches with a back problem last February, so depth behind him is a fair concern. Yet Liverpool sit fourth, a point behind second-placed Brighton after Sunday’s 4-0 win over Manchester United, and only eighth in the Champions League table after losing to Fenerbahce. January minutes will decide those races, and Ouazane has four Eredivisie starts and numbers that clash with Iraola’s pressing.

His lifelong Anfield dream and Ward’s record of targeting elite teenagers give Liverpool an edge, so they should push. #1489. Marco Rose delivers injury update as Bournemouth make Junior Kroupi, Ben Gannon-Doak Europa League squad alteration

By Ben Sully | 25 Nov 2026 19:11

Bournemouth boss Marco Rose has confirmed Junior Kroupi has been reinstated to the Europa League squad ahead of Thursday’s clash against Celta Vigo.

The France international was initially named in the Europa League squad despite undergoing foot surgery in the summer.

However, Kroupi’s absence allowed Bournemouth to use UEFA’s temporary injury replacement rule to include Ben Gannon-Doak for the first four games in the league phase.

Kroupi returned to action last month, but as a result of Gannon-Doak’s inclusion in the Europa League squad, he was unable to feature in the 3-1 win over Sparta Prague at the start of the month.

Rose has now confirmed Kroupi has been brought back into the Europa League squad, meaning Gannon-Doak will drop out for the final four league phase matches unless there are any further injury replacement opportunities.

Alex Scott is also available to make his first Europa League appearance since matchday one after returning from a thigh injury with a substitute appearance in Saturday’s 2-0 win over Nottingham Forest.

"Everyone is ready,” Rose said. "We have no new injuries ahead of tomorrow's game.

“We are glad to have Alex and Junior back and available."

When asked whether the pair will start in Vigo, Rose said: "It could be possible, but also maybe not. We will see"

In regard to absentees, the Cherries are without the injured trio of Julian Araujo, Juanlu Sanchez and Alex Toth.

Bournemouth are currently enjoying the longest winning run in the club's history after recording a ninth consecutive victory in all competitions at the weekend.

They also boast a perfect record in their maiden European campaign, having won their four league phase matches by a combined 11-2 scoreline.

As a result, they head into matchday five in second spot in the Europa League league phase and five points clear of the teams sitting just outside the top eight.

#1488. Juventus Next Gen beaten 4-0 at Lecco and left third from bottom

Juventus Next Gen were beaten 4-0 at Lecco in Serie C Girone A, with three of the goals coming after half-time. Coach Massimo Brambilla admitted his young side give goals away too easily, and the table now reflects a long poor run.

At the Stadio Rigamonti-Ceppi, the manner of the defeat was as worrying as the scoreline.

The opener set the tone. Lecco needed only six minutes to go ahead. Casarotto ran through the middle, got past Corradi and beat goalkeeper Mangiapoco. Lecco held that single-goal lead until half-time.

Next Gen did have one clear opening before the break. In the 40th minute, Grelaud shot from near the penalty spot. Vettorel turned the effort over for a corner.

The second half was one-way traffic. Capello made it 2-0 in the 50th minute, and Manetti added a third in the 56th. Capello struck from close range after the goalkeeper parried Pellegrino’s second attempt. Murillo’s goal in the 72nd minute summed up the match. Mangiapoco erred as Juventus built from the back, and Murillo pounced.

The hosts are in strong form. This was their second 4-0 win in a row, after beating Dolomiti Bellunesi by the same score. Lecco have now scored 15 goals in four games.

Massimo Brambilla did not hide from the problems. He told TuttoMercatoWeb that his side struggled against Lecco’s high press. His players found it hard to keep the ball against a team pressing hard and man-to-man.

The coach also admitted that coming back became difficult after the second goal. He said his players must improve how they read the game and stop giving away goals so easily.

The table makes the warning sharper. Brambilla’s side sit third from bottom after the defeat, having won just one of their last 12 matches.

The result also matters beyond Serie C. Carnevali has put the youth sector at the centre of the club’s plans.

One player supporters will watch is Destiny Elimoghale, who came off the bench at Lecco. Next Gen had started in a 3-5-2, with Durmisi and Merola in attack. Elimoghale replaced Durmisi in the 40th minute of the second half. The forward was born in 2009. His new contract, announced on 3 November, runs until 30 June 2029.

Elimoghale was called up to the first-team squad for the first time on 17 September 2026. That call-up came for the opening Europa League league-phase match against NEC.

The next opponents arrive in good spirits. Treviso beat Novara 2-0 in round 13. Romeo scored in the 24th minute, and Paganini added the second in the 59th.

The next test comes quickly. Next Gen host Treviso in round 14 on Sunday 15 November at 17:30. A trip to Giana Erminio follows on Saturday 21 November, at the same kick-off time.

#1486. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

Anthony Gordon created Champions League history in Barcelona's 4-1 success over Sabah in the league stage of the competition on Wednesday night.

The England international scored twice in Azerbaijan to play a leading role in Hansi Flick's side securing an impressive win in the European Cup.

Gordon has now scored six Champions League goals in Azerbaijan, which is the most any English player has netted in away games in one country in the tournament.

Four of the attacker's goals in Azerbaijan came against Qarabag during his time with Newcastle United, before scoring twice more against Sabah.

#1482. Jose Mourinho sends clear Real Madrid message to Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger after PSV double substitution

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 19:56

Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has offered a revealing assessment of his defensive hierarchy after substituting Eder Militao and Antonio Rudiger at half-time during Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven.

Los Blancos were trailing 1-0 at the Santiago Bernabeu when Mourinho made three changes at the interval, withdrawing both experienced centre-backs alongside Aurelien Tchouameni. Ibrahima Konate and Dean Huijsen entered in defence, while Jude Bellingham replaced the French midfielder.

The decision preceded a remarkable turnaround. Madrid scored five unanswered goals in the second half, with Bellingham, Federico Valverde, Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Junior contributing to a victory that maintained their perfect Champions League record after five matches.

Although Mourinho insisted that the improvement was primarily down to a collective change in mentality, his explanation for replacing Militao and Rudiger offered an insight into why Konate and Huijsen have established themselves as his preferred central-defensive partnership.

The Portuguese coach acknowledged that the two younger defenders currently benefit from greater match sharpness, while identifying specific qualities that make them particularly valuable to his system.

Speaking to Movistar after the match, Mourinho explained that his decision had been influenced by several factors, including the yellow cards shown to Rudiger and Tchouameni during the opening period.

"A bit of everything," he said when asked whether the substitutions were motivated by fitness, disciplinary concerns or a desire to change the game.

"We had two players on yellow cards in a game against some very quick players, which was a risk."

However, Mourinho's subsequent assessment was arguably more significant for the two defenders who had been withdrawn.

"Obviously, the two centre-backs who have been playing more regularly are in a better rhythm," he continued.

"Dean is our best player at bringing the ball out from the back, Konate is playing pretty well... and I thought those changes could help us."

Those comments underline the advantages currently enjoyed by Huijsen and Konate, who have become Mourinho's regular pairing since the beginning of the campaign.

Huijsen's ability to progress possession from defence is particularly important in a Madrid side expected to dominate the ball, while Konate provides the physical presence and defensive intensity required when the team presses high.

Both qualities were evident in the second half against PSV, when Madrid pushed their defensive line forward and prevented the Dutch visitors from progressing comfortably through midfield.

Mourinho nevertheless resisted the suggestion that his defensive substitutions alone had transformed the contest.

The former Chelsea and Manchester United manager also credited Bellingham's introduction and a collective improvement in pressing, explaining that his players had struggled to win individual battles before the interval.

"The second half was a question of mentality," Mourinho said. "We made changes, yes, and Jude is a different kind of player who gives us what we lacked in the first half, but collectively we were better in the second half."

His explanation makes it difficult to interpret the removal of Militao and Rudiger as an outright rejection of either player. Yet publicly highlighting the superior rhythm and individual qualities of their competitors offers a clear indication of the current pecking order.

The situation is particularly delicate for Rudiger, whose contract expires in June 2027.

The 33-year-old German has found regular opportunities difficult to secure under Mourinho, and reports in Spain have suggested that Real Madrid are increasingly unlikely to offer him another extension.

His experience remains an asset, particularly across a demanding season involving several competitions, but his reduced role raises questions about whether he will remain at the Bernabeu beyond next summer.

The Brazil international remains under contract until June 2028, although his recent career has been disrupted by two serious anterior cruciate ligament injuries and further muscular problems.

He has played only five minutes in La Liga this season, with his Champions League appearances providing most of his opportunities to regain competitive sharpness.

Tuesday's meeting with PSV represented another chance to demonstrate his readiness for a more prominent role. Instead, his involvement ended after 45 minutes as Mourinho turned to the partnership that has largely carried Madrid's defence this season.

The Brazilian's limited playing time makes the manager's comments about rhythm particularly relevant. Regaining his previous level requires regular appearances, but those opportunities are difficult to obtain while Konate and Huijsen continue to perform.

Huijsen's emergence has already complicated Militao's attempts to recover a starting place, with the Spain international establishing himself as a central figure in Mourinho's defensive plans.

Konate, meanwhile, has made a strong impression following his arrival from Liverpool, offering the combination of athleticism and defensive aggression that the Portuguese coach values.

The two established internationals therefore face different uncertainties. Rudiger must consider his future as his contract approaches its conclusion, while Militao has more time remaining on his deal but needs to demonstrate that he can compete consistently for a starting position.

Mourinho has not announced plans to sell either defender, and Tuesday's substitutions should not be regarded as confirmation of their departures.

However, the manager's unusually explicit assessment of his centre-backs has reinforced the challenge facing both players: Konate and Huijsen currently possess the match rhythm, tactical qualities and established partnership that make them difficult to displace.

#1481. Thuram and Locatelli absences leave Juventus midfield thin for four games in 12 days

Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

The table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

#1479. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#1478. Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

#1477. ‘Mozart of maths’ Terence Tao is your guide to what underpins reality

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Itai Yanai is a professor in the Institute for Systems Genetics, New York University Grossman School of Medicine, New York City.

After centuries of debate, a mathematical proof of the most efficient way to stack balls was produced only in 1998. Credit: Getty

Six Maths Essentials: How to Model the World Terence Tao Pelican

Can knowing about central principles in mathematics help us to understand our world? Leading mathematician Terence Tao — who has been called the Mozart of maths — explains how it can in his latest book, Six Maths Essentials.

Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world

Can maths survive AI? Fields medallist Terence Tao calls for a ‘Maths 2.0’ world

For Tao, the six concepts are the building blocks of reality that together provide an opportunity to better understand it. They are, he writes: “numbers as the gateway to quantitative thinking, algebra as the gateway to abstraction, geometry as a way to go beyond what we can see, probability as a tool to navigate uncertainty with rigorous thinking, analysis as a means to tame the very large or very small, and dynamics as the mathematics of change”.

Each is described with elegant minimalism, consistent with Tao’s vocation of writing concise mathematical proofs. In its brevity, the book evokes physicist Richard Feynman’s Six Easy Pieces (1994), which explains fundamental physics concepts to the layperson. Similarly, the beauty of Tao’s book is seeing maths through his eyes, describing its spirit as well as generalizing across the discipline.

For instance, Tao describes how artificial intelligence inspires awe and magic — it easily lives up to science-fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke’s famous statement that “any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic”. But AI has a dark side, too. It can lead us to become superstitious and think that the tool cares about us, or to develop a sense of fear that we wouldn’t know how to live if it malfunctioned.

Tao makes the case that maths has played an important part in the story of humanity. We meet famous mathematicians such as ninth-century Islamic astronomer Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī, who pioneered algebra, following in the footsteps of the ancient Babylonians, and gave his name to the Latin form of the term algorithm. Others solved real-world problems, from calculating the distance between Earth and the Sun to understanding the 2008 global financial crisis.

We learn about mathematicians who overcame the desire of philosophers such as Immanuel Kant to pigeonhole geometry into a single ‘true’ concept, instead finding that there is a plurality of connected geometries. Other mathematicians revealed the laws of chance through their passion for gambling.

AI has transformed maths — this is how we got here

AI has transformed maths — this is how we got here

Tao invokes hardly any equations, opting instead for intuitive explanations. It is through this same intuition, Tao argues, that children work out that there is no highest number, thus deducing the concept of infinity. He discusses the elegance of algebra and its ability to solve many problems without requiring a tailored equation for each application. This generalizability, he notes, is what distinguishes maths from organic chemistry — which was his least favourite subject in school, he writes, because it required memorizing disparate facts without organizing principles like those found in maths.

He is at his best explaining difficult topics to the public. On analysis, he writes that there are both hard and soft aspects, corresponding to quantitative and qualitative modes. He calls analysis the accountant of maths: “auditing and proving which techniques work under what circumstances”.

He uses mathematician John Conway’s Game of Life to demonstrate the need to study dynamics. In this game, simple rules are applied to a matrix of elements that are either ‘on’ or ‘off’ as they unfold into complex patterns. The grid functions as a rudimentary yet, in principle, fully functional computer.

John Conway used games to transform mathematics.Credit: Dith Pran/NYT/Redux/eyevine

Importantly, Tao conveys how mathematicians think as they discover new maths. He distinguishes the ‘cold’ maths found in textbooks from the active maths that happens as mathematicians explore fresh domains. For example, he describes how Carl Friedrich Gauss imagined what it would be like to be on the surface of a sphere — a view that led to his “remarkable theorem” on the properties of curvature, proved in 1827.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03720-w

#1476. “If there can be a way out” – Moretto states Milan have no intention of offering Tomori a renewal

It seems we are heading into the final year of Fikayo Tomori’s playing relationship with AC Milan, with talk of a renewal silent.

Next year, at the end of June, Tomori’s deal expires and if nothing is done before then, his six-year spell with the club will come to an end.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It’s been an up-and-down season for the Englishman, especially after he was included in the ‘bomb squad’ through the mercato. However, he was needed back in the squad and reintegrated.

Despite showing this fight, though, it seems unlikely that he’ll be rewarded with a new deal. There are plans to invest heavily in the club next year and the defender isn’t seen as a pillar of the team, let alone the defence. So a renewal isn’t being focused on.

As Matteo Moretto told viewers on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel, Tomori previously had a chance at a renewal. However, that now seems to have gone, as MilanNews relays.

“There’s a before and after regarding Tomori. In my opinion, if Massimiliano Allegri had remained on the Milan bench, perhaps in that case there could have been a chance of a renewal for Tomori.

“Then there was the slightly peculiar way Milan handled the Tomori situation. Tomori is a player who has always been absolutely professional and deeply loves the Milan shirt; he has always shown all his commitment.

“It’s true, he was sidelined; Milan tried to find solutions on the way out right in the last days of the transfer window. His contract expires in 2027.

“There were discussions underway for the renewal when Allegri was on the bench; then, with time and with the succession of certain events, this type of renewal was no longer discussed.

“To date, the negotiations are absolutely at a standstill. There is no dialogue between the parties and I repeat, Tomori’s contract expires in 2027.

“We’ll see if in January there can be a way out, perhaps with the payment of compensation to Milan, or if it will reach zero in June, but as of today there is no trace of a possible renewal.”

#1475. Zhegrova plays 82 minutes in Kosovo’s 0-0 with Israel before Dublin decider for second

With Edon Zhegrova in the starting line-up, ten-man Kosovo held Israel to a goalless draw, a result that leaves them second in Nations League Group B3. The run-out gives a Juventus forward who rarely starts for his club valuable match fitness while Pierre Kalulu is injured.

In Pristina, the Juventus forward Edon Zhegrova was Kosovo’s main attacker against Israel.

Zhegrova tested Israel’s defence a couple of times in the first half but faded after the break, according to TuttoJuve. Dion Kacuri came on in his place.

Below Kosovo, Ireland have 5 points and Israel 3. Austria beat the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on the same Saturday.

Kosovo’s campaign has been uneven. They opened by beating the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on 24 September. Three days later they lost 3-1 away to Austria on 27 September. On matchday 3, they had also drawn 0-0 with Israel.

The final round pairs the Republic of Ireland with Kosovo and Israel with Austria. That leaves Ireland, sitting just below Kosovo, hosting the side directly above them. Zhegrova is set to be central to Kosovo’s hopes of holding on to second place.

For Juventus, the significance lies in the minutes. Zhegrova has started only once since joining the club. He sits low in Spalletti’s pecking order and has mostly featured in short spells off the bench.

More than 80 minutes as Kosovo’s focal point gives him match fitness. That could prove useful before Juventus face Venezia in Serie A and Omonia in the Europa League.

The squad is stretched. Scans at J|medical on 9 November found a low-grade injury to Pierre Kalulu’s left biceps femoris. The defender had felt muscle discomfort in his left thigh after the draw at Fiorentina. France withdrew him from their squad. The midfield is also short of bodies.

Spalletti has made clear he sees potential in the winger. “Edon se si completa un po’ può diventare un crack,” the coach said. If Edon rounds out his game a little, he can become a star.

We draw 0–0 with Kosovo in the UEFA Nations League. pic.twitter.com/SSS4UTPpw4

— ISRAEL FA (@ISRAELFA) November 14, 2026

Other clubs are paying attention too. Near the end of the summer window, Al-Ittihad made a move for the winger, and Monaco are also interested, Eurosport Italia reported. A strong finish to the international window would do his standing no harm, in Turin or elsewhere.

First comes Dublin. Kick-off at the Aviva Stadium is at 7.45pm UK time, with second place in the group at stake.

#1474. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

INS:Illan Meslier from Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis from Club Brugge, £34mBruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, £75m

Piero Hincapie’s move from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent this summer.

August 1- Girona 1 Arsenal 4August 5-  Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3Today- Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (Emirates Cup)August 12- Arsenal vs ComoAugust 16- Arsenal vs Manchester City (Community Shield)

🚨 STARTING XI VS ARSENAL 🚨 pic.twitter.com/Wk6QPOGDnW

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️🧱 Gabriel at the back©️ Odegaard skippers the side😤 Gyokeres leads the line More pre-season minutes in the tank - let's do this, Gunners ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/FQwOjCDAje

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.
